To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the pelagic microbial community composition was strongly affected by the input of benthic biofilms, (b) the pelagic viral community composition was not affected by the biofilm input, (c) biofilms were a major source of organic matter for the pelagic food web, (d) the biofilm input stimulated the pelagic bacterial growth, and (e) the biofilm viral input stimulated bacterial mortality.

the biofilm is the main source of pelagic bacteria in the mudflat, and the pelagic bacteria are a major source of pelagic viruses in this environment.

the biofilm input is a crucial driver for the pelagic food web functioning and that the biofilm is a source of both dissolved and particulate organic carbon for pelagic bacteria, which in turn are a food source for heterotrophic protists and viruses.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benthic biofilms of intertidal mud flats are a source of organic matter and microbial particles that are released into the water and contribute to the pelagic microbial loop.
the microbial loop and the viral loop are coupled in the pelagic ecosystem, but the coupling is stronger in the summer than in the winter.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbial communities in the mudflat are not static but dynamic, with seasonal changes in the microbial community structure and function.
the microbial loop in the water column of an intertidal ecosystem is strongly influenced by the input of benthic biofilms.
the pelagic viral and bacterial loops are not only driven by phytoplankton, but also by the benthic biofilms.
